title: SQ-DM: Accelerating Diffusion Models with Aggressive Quantization and Temporal Sparsity
problem: Diffusion models require many inference steps for high-quality generation, limiting practical deployment; aggressive quantization and sparsity are difficult to exploit due to time-variant sparsity patterns that vary across channels and timesteps.
motivation: Accelerating diffusion model inference is critical for practical deployment; combining quantization with channel-aware temporal sparsity offers significant speedup potential if hardware can handle dynamic sparsity.
method: SQ-DM applies 4-bit aggressive weight and activation quantization combined with channel-specific activation sparsity that evolves per timestep; a custom accelerator with heterogeneous mixed-precision dense-sparse architecture, channel-last mapping, and timestep-aware sparsity detection handles the dynamic patterns efficiently.
key_novelty: Aggressive 4-bit quantization combined with dynamic channel-specific temporal sparsity detection and specialized hardware support for heterogeneous dense-sparse acceleration.
contributions: 4-bit quantization technique with superior generation quality compared to existing 4-bit methods
Identification of channel-specific temporal sparsity patterns across timesteps
Custom accelerator with heterogeneous mixed-precision dense-sparse dataflow
6.91x speedup and 51.5% energy reduction compared to dense accelerators
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation on diffusion models without broader generative model coverage.
primary_theme: Aggressive quantization with dynamic temporal sparsity for diffusion model acceleration
